key_insight: InterMimicGen turns scarce human-object interaction data into a self-improving training loop for humanoid robots. By letting robot motions and a tracking policy refine each other, it scales humanoid loco-manipulation beyond one-shot imitation.
problem_solved: Human-object interaction data is rich but hard to use for robots because it is sparse, diverse, and not directly executable. The paper addresses how to convert such data into usable humanoid motion supervision for coordinated walking, reaching, and hand-object manipulation.
method: Consolidate multiple motion-capture human-object interaction datasets into a unified training set.
Retarget human motions to humanoid robot references while preserving whole-body coordination and dexterous hand-object contact.
Use a self-evolving loop where generated robot motions and a tracking policy improve each other over time, expanding usable motion data for loco-manipulation.
impact: This approach can help practitioners build more capable humanoid control systems with less hand-engineered data collection. It is especially useful for scaling imitation learning to complex, real-world tasks that require both locomotion and manipulation.

paper_title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
paper_authors: Yucheng Zhang, Sirui Xu, Jinhong Li, Liuyu Bian, Anatulya Nandi
